legend: A well-circumscribed ulcerated lesion involving the oral mucosa.

The polymorphic infiltrate of EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcer exhibits a mixture of cell types including small lymphocytes, plasma cells, histiocytes, eosinophils, and large transformed cells resembling HRS cells (<<30874>>). Large immunoblasts and HRS-like cells in a mixed inflammatory background may be a prominent feature of EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcer (cutaneous localization) (<<30878>>). Angioinvasion can be present (oral cavity localization) (<<30875>>). In situ hybridization for EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER) shows the presence of numerous EBV-positive cells in small and large lymphoid cells, highlighting HRS-like cells (cutaneous localization) (<<30879>>).

diagnosis: EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcer involving the tonsil
legend: Extensive mucosal ulceration and necrosis accompanied by a heterogeneous infiltrate in a case of EBVMCU involving the tonsil.
